To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) TP53 and PIK3 pathway genes are the most frequently and distinctively altered genes in breast tumors, 2) these genes are altered in a mutually exclusive manner in most tumors, and 3) TP53 and the PIK3 pathway mutations are significantly associated to hormone receptors status but independent of HER-2 expression.
the TP53 and PIK3 pathway genes are frequently mutated in different breast tumor subtypes and that these mutation profiles can predict the tumor hormone status.
TP53 and genes of the PIK3 pathway (PIKCA and PTEN and AKT1) are mutated in a large proportion of individual tumors and that their mutation patterns are associated with hormone receptor expression.
